gloss: to voice an objection; to raise a protest

definitions.gloss: to voice an objection; to raise a protest; to object
definitions.explanation: To formally or publicly express disagreement or opposition to a decision, plan, or statement. Used in legal, political, and everyday contexts when someone speaks up against something.

examples.japanese: {異議|いぎ}を{唱|とな}える{人|ひと}はいませんか。
{住民|じゅうみん}たちが{計画|けいかく}に{異議|いぎ}を{唱|とな}えた。
examples.english: The residents voiced objections to the plan.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{会議|かいぎ}で{一人|ひとり}だけ{異議|いぎ}を{唱|とな}えたが、{多数決|たすうけつ}で{否決|ひけつ}された。
examples.english: He was the only one to raise an objection at the meeting, but it was voted down by majority.

notes: A set phrase combining {異議|いぎ} (objection/dissent) + を + {唱|とな}える (to advocate/voice). Common in meetings, legal proceedings, and public discourse. In parliamentary or meeting settings, the chair may ask {異議|いぎ}はありませんか (Are there any objections?) or {異議|いぎ}なしと{認|みと}めます (No objections noted; motion carried). Related expressions: {異議|いぎ}を{申|もう}し{立|た}てる (to file an objection, more formal/legal), {反対|はんたい}する (to oppose, more general).
